rules.cite: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017) § 1
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers with DND funding or land, or income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.

exemptions.description: Direct relationship between conviction and housing sought, unreasonable risk to safety of others, or current criminal behavior

key_values.name: conviction_lookback
key_values.text: A conviction more than 5 years old

rules.quote:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.
relations_hint:
Where federal or state law imposes a criminal history requirement that conflicts with a 
requirement of this guidance, the federal or state law preempts this policy.
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not apply blanket denials based on arrests or convictions and must review applicants case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, judicially relieved convictions, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old, subject to exceptions.
rules.title: Fair chance criminal history screening limits

rules.cite: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017) § Credit
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers with DND funding or land, or income-restricted inclusionary units.
rules.quote:
The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing    
applications.
rules.requirement: Covered agents may not use credit scores to approve or deny applications. Credit history may be considered only in lieu of rental history when rental history is unavailable.
rules.title: No credit score use in screening
